summary: Discovery call to understand Atlas Aerospace requirements for an on-prem, air-gapped deployment of Redwood Private. Key concerns: offline update process, approved hardware, encryption/KMS approach, network egress restrictions, and who operates the stack. Redwood AE+SE walked through options (private control plane + air-gapped image updates, or fully offline control plane) and proposed a pilot with a small cluster. Security wants proof of audit logs, HSM integration, and an approved patching workflow.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-31
Start: 14:30 PDT
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Tom R (Atlas CTO), Priya M (Head of ML), Carlos V (Security), Alicia P (Infra)

Summary (auto): quick discovery on air-gapped deployment, offline updates, HW constraints, pilot scope

[00:00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, we got your agenda, we want to make sure we cover the air gap constraints and the pilot. quick intro, i'm maya and samir will cover technicals.
[00:00:08] Tom (Atlas CTO): Thanks Maya, yeah we run all production in an air-gapped colocation, no outbound internet allowed except through our change-controlled proxy, and most updates have to go via signed media. we want to understand options: do you support fully offline control plane or do you need connectivity to redwood hosted control plane?
[00:00:24] Samir (Redwood SE): Great question. short answer: we support both models. for fully offline we offer an onprem package that includes a private control plane image and an operator runbook. updates can be shipped as signed images or via an approved USB procedure. for semi-isolated setups we can run a control plane inside your VPC with egress to our update endpoints via a constrained proxy.
[00:00:40] Priya (Head of ML): When you say image updates, is that for the runtime only or also model weights? we run large models — a lot of weights are tens or hundreds of GBs and our datacenter policies limit removable storage.
[00:00:51] Samir (Redwood SE): both are supported. typically weights are handled as model bundles, signed and checksumed. customers can host them on internal object storage (S3-compatible) in the air-gapped network. for weight distribution we support a staged import: bring the bundle in via secure media to a designated import node which validates signatures and replicates locally.
[00:01:08] Carlos (Security): we need to see KMS/HSM support. keys cannot leave our HSMs and bring-your-own-key is a must. also audit logs must be tamper-evident and integrated with our SIEM.
[00:01:17] Maya (Redwood AE): absolutely, we have options. our Private deployment supports customer-managed KMS/HSM. logs can be exported to your syslog/siem, and we provide signed log archives for forensic purposes. i'll attach the security integration doc after the call.
[00:01:29] Alicia (Infra): hardware — what GPUs are supported? we have a mixed fleet: a couple of A100 80GB, some older A40s and one skylake host with 32GB cards. our procurement might not replace everything immediately.
[00:01:39] Samir (Redwood SE): Redwood runtime supports an array of nvidia cards. recommended for high-throughput LLM serving is A100 or H100; A40s are ok for smaller models or quantized workflows. we can provide quantization profiles; we also do kernel selection based on arch. note: older cards may not support latest fused kernels so perf will vary. could you share the exact model strings and driver versions?
[00:01:59] Tom (Atlas CTO): yes, we'll share inventory. also blackout windows for maintenance are tightly controlled, makes scheduling a pilot tricky.
[00:02:06] Priya (Head of ML): on the model side we have two candidates: LlamaX-70B (open) and an in-house 13B fine-tuned model. latency targets: sub-100ms for quick retrieval workflows is preferred but throughput is more important for batch scoring. pricing and cost per token will be a factor vs the in-house stack.
[00:02:23] Maya (Redwood AE): thanks, we'll include cost estimates for both latency-optimized and throughput-optimized configs. for onprem pilots we typically recommend starting with a small cluster (2-4 GPUs) for validation then scale.
[00:02:33] Carlos (Security): we also need to understand software patching. in an air-gapped env we can't have automatic updates. what's your recommended patch cadence and can you provide signed patches and roll-back capability?
[00:02:42] Samir (Redwood SE): yes signed releases and rollback images are standard. we produce SHA256 signed artifacts; your operator imports them to an import node which validates signatures before applying. we also support reproducible container images and delta patches to reduce data transfer.
[00:02:54] Tom (Atlas CTO): who operates the infra day-to-day? your managed option or we run it ourselves? liability for uptime in our contracts matters.
[00:03:02] Maya (Redwood AE): two models: customer-operated (we hand over images, ops playbook, and provide 24/7 support SLA optionally) or Redwood-managed where we run the stack in your datacenter under a managed services agreement and integrate to your ticketing and on-call. managed has additional fees but reduces your ops burden.
[00:03:18] Priya (Head of ML): for the POC we prefer to operate ourselves but want Redwood to validate perf and help with tuning. is there tooling for continuous batching, KV cache priming, and trace level metrics?
[00:03:28] Samir (Redwood SE): yes runtime has continuous batching, KV cache management, and telemetry. we can enable token-level cost and latency breakdowns in the console. in air-gapped mode telemetry is stored locally and can be exported to your observability stack.
[00:03:40] Tom (Atlas CTO): any tradeoffs if we go fully air-gapped vs hybrid?
[00:03:44] Samir (Redwood SE): main tradeoffs: convenience of remote updates and telemetry vs control and compliance. fully air-gapped increases operational overhead for you (manual updates, import process) and can slow reactive patches. hybrid with a restricted egress channel gives near-equal control but faster patching. cost-wise, onprem licensing and managed services are usually higher than hosted.
[00:04:02] Priya (Head of ML): curious about fallback strategies. if a model version fails under load, can you automatically route to a smaller/quantized variant?
[00:04:09] Samir (Redwood SE): yes we support routing policies and automatic fallback to pre-provisioned model variants. that logic runs in the runtime and is compatible with private deployments. we'd need the variant images imported and pinned.
[00:04:19] Carlos (Security): what about compliance artifacts — SOC2 reports, pen test results, third-party audit history?
[00:04:24] Maya (Redwood AE): we'll send SOC2 summary, pen test highlights redacted, and the third-party audit attestations. full artifacts can be made available under NDA.
[00:04:33] Tom (Atlas CTO): timeline: we need a pilot in Q2, ideally in April. can you commit to that?
[00:04:38] Maya (Redwood AE): yes target week of 2026-04-13 as discussed. we'll start with hardware checklist and a short security questionnaire so we can scope the image build and import process.
[00:04:46] Priya (Head of ML): one more question re: model licensing and redistrib — if we bring open models vs commercial models, any special handling?
[00:04:52] Samir (Redwood SE): open models are straightforward; for commercial models we need to review licensing for onprem use — some vendors restrict offline deployments. we can help with license review as part of the POC.
[00:05:00] Alicia (Infra): what's the expected disk and network footprint for model bundles?
[00:05:04] Samir (Redwood SE): a 70B dense model with 16-bit will be ~140-160GB weights; quantized 4-bit ~30-40GB. during import we recommend a staging node with at least 2x the model size for unpacking and validation. network wise delta patches are smaller; full image transfers will require capacity planning.
[00:05:18] Maya (Redwood AE): ok wrapping up — i'll follow up with the security docs and the SOC2/ISO summaries. Samir will send the hardware checklist and reference architecture. Tom you'll share GPU inventory. we'll schedule the on-site workshop.
[00:05:30] Tom (Atlas CTO): thanks all, that sounds good.
[00:05:33] Maya (Redwood AE): thanks everyone, meeting adjourned.

Notes on transcription quality: a few words mis-heard (skylake host may be "sky-lake" in transcript), proper nouns may vary.
